content.title: Nvidia, bitcoin and other falling stars drag the US stock market lower
content.summary: The U.S. stock market sank Monday as Nvidia and other superstars created by the frenzy around artificial-intelligence  technology dimmed some more.  Nvidia was the heaviest weight on the market, as it’s often been in its last couple of tumultuous weeks. The chip company fell 1.8%, while losses for other AI winners included a 6.4% slide for Super Micro Computer.

content.title: 3 Growth Stocks Insiders Are Betting On
content.summary: As the U.S. market navigates a period of mixed performance, with technology shares rebounding while the Dow Jones Industrial Average faces declines, investors are keenly observing insider activity as a potential indicator of confidence in growth stocks. In this environment, companies with high insider ownership can be particularly appealing, reflecting strong internal belief in their future prospects despite broader market volatility.

content.title: Tech Selloff Flips to a Rally. The Dow Is Lagging Behind.
content.summary: The tech stock selloff flipped into rally mode on Friday as Wall Street finally stepped in to buy the dip.  The Nasdaq Composite rallied 0.8%.  The Dow was down 108 points, or 0.2%, after dropping more than 500 points earlier in the day.

content.title: Nasdaq Could Mark Biggest Comeback Since April. Wall Street Is Buying the Dip in Nvidia and Other AI Stocks.
content.summary: The Nasdaq Composite clawed back to positive territory as a handful of key AI stocks like Nvidia rallied off their lows.  The S&P 500 was down 0.2%, though only 147 stocks in the index were in positive territory.  Nvidia turned positive and was up 0.5% in recent trading.
